title: Inside your radio
blurb: The big idea before the cards.

lines.caption: Most ham radios are transceivers: a transmitter and a receiver in one box.
lines.label: two radios in one

lines.caption: Inside is a chain of blocks, and each block does one job. First, an oscillator generates a signal at one specific frequency.
lines.label: makes the signal

lines.caption: Modulation combines your speech with that signal, which is called the carrier.
lines.label: adds your voice

lines.caption: A mixer converts a signal from one frequency to another.
lines.label: changes the frequency

lines.caption: A power amplifier makes the signal stronger on its way to the antenna.
lines.label: adds power

lines.caption: Coming the other way, a good receiver is sensitive enough to detect weak signals, and selective enough to pick out just one.
lines.label: sensitive and selective
